title: docs(core,i18n,plugin-report): each display-locale contract names the caller it governs
body:
Fixes #10098
Clause-②: no

## What this does

The ruling on this card (comment 5814449943, maintainer 「同意」) asks for each of the two declared display-locale contracts to name the caller it governs, and for each to point at the other. That is what this PR does. It changes comments and adds one changeset. No module's behaviour changes.

- **`@object-ui/core`, `DisplayNumberFormatOptions.locale`** (`packages/core/src/utils/number-display.ts`). The existing `undefined` paragraph is unchanged, byte for byte. A new paragraph says four things:
  - The rule is written for a non-React display caller that has no tag.
  - For that caller, the runtime default is the viewer's own environment, which is the honest locale for a user-facing display.
  - A malformed tag ends up in the same place, through the retry in `formatDisplayNumber`.
  - A React renderer follows `useDisplayLocale` instead. The paragraph names that hook's package and path.
- **`@object-ui/i18n`, `useDisplayLocale`** (`packages/i18n/src/useDisplayLocale.ts`). The existing text of step 3 (the `'en'` last resort) is unchanged, byte for byte, because plugin-report quotes it verbatim. A new paragraph limits that rule to a React renderer whose provider chain yields no tag at all. It names `DisplayNumberFormatOptions.locale` in `@object-ui/core` as the rule for the other caller.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-report`, `formatNumberInDisplayLocale`** (`packages/plugin-report/src/displayLocale.ts`). The re-check below found that this note contradicts the scoped `core` wording: it called core's retry, which drops the tag, "the other wrong answer the contract quoted above names". I rewrote the note to say that each retry follows its own package's declared contract. Only the comment changed.

The cross-references are plain text that names the package, the symbol and the path. `{@link}` would not resolve across this boundary: `core` is the React-free engine and cannot import `i18n`, and neither file imports the other's symbol. The one `{@link}` I added points to `formatDisplayNumber`, which is in the same module. The new text cites no line numbers.

## The retry re-check (the ruling's last clause)

`formatNumberInLocale` is defined in one place only: `packages/core/src/utils/dataset-format.ts`. It is a module-private adapter over `formatDisplayNumber`, and the `catch` in `formatDisplayNumber` retries with the locale dropped. `packages/plugin-report/src/displayLocale.ts` neither defines nor wraps it. That file has its own separate function, `formatNumberInDisplayLocale`, which retries with `'en'`.

I measured this myself on this branch's source, with a tsx probe run from the worktree root (the probe is not committed). The malformed tag `zh_CN` and the well-formed control `zh-CN` went through the same exported paths. I ran each tag under two runtime defaults, set with `LC_ALL`. The table shows `formatMeasure(1234.5, '0.00', 'CNY', undefined, tag)` for core and `formatNumberInDisplayLocale(1234.5, tag, CNY options)` for plugin-report:

| runtime default | tag | bare `Intl.NumberFormat(tag)` | core output | core renders in | plugin-report output | plugin-report renders in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| en-US | `zh_CN` | throws `RangeError` | `CN¥1,234.50` | en-US (runtime default) | `CN¥1,234.50` | en |
| en-US | `zh-CN` | ok, resolves zh-CN | `¥1,234.50` | zh-CN | `¥1,234.50` | zh-CN |
| de-DE | `zh_CN` | throws `RangeError` | `1.234,50 CN¥` | de-DE (runtime default) | `CN¥1,234.50` | en |
| de-DE | `zh-CN` | ok, resolves zh-CN | `¥1,234.50` | zh-CN | `¥1,234.50` | zh-CN |

The CNY rendering is what tells zh-CN apart from en. Plain decimals cannot: zh-CN and en both render `1,234,567.89`. `formatDimensionValue(1234567.891, 'zh_CN')` gives `1.234.567,89` under de-DE and `1,234,567.89` under en-US, so it follows the runtime default the same way.

**What the table shows:** core's retry drops the malformed tag and falls back to the runtime default, which changes with `LC_ALL`. The card relayed this claim without measuring it; the measurement confirms it. The well-formed control does not change. The plugin-report function lands on `'en'` whatever the runtime default is.

**How that compares with the scoped wording:** core's retry lands exactly where core's scoped contract puts a caller with no usable tag, which is the runtime default (the viewer's environment). The comments beside that retry say so and do not contradict the scope, so I left them unchanged:
- `formatDisplayNumber`: "Retry WITHOUT the locale"
- the `formatNumberInLocale` docblock
- the note in the currency `catch` of `formatMeasure`

Only plugin-report's note contradicted the scoped wording, and I rewrote it as a comment.

## Proof that no executable byte changed

- A filter that lists changed lines that are not comments prints nothing (grep exit 1):
  `git diff -U0 BASE -- packages | grep -E '^[+-]' | grep -vE '^(\+\+\+|---) ' | grep -vE '^[+-][[:space:]]*(\*|/\*\*|\*/|//)'`
- I transpiled each touched module at BASE (`8b1f0661`) and at this branch's HEAD with TypeScript `transpileModule` and `removeComments: true`. The sources differ, but the output is byte-identical on both sides. The sha256 prefixes are `959e7c0be2fc6f9a` (number-display), `838246c545c47ff0` (useDisplayLocale) and `11c182aa22edd48f` (displayLocale).
- `en-US` appears 0 times in the added lines of the diff and 0 times in the changeset.

## Changeset: patch, not an empty frontmatter

`.changeset/10098-locale-contracts-name-caller.md` declares `patch` for `@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/plugin-report`. The presence gate requires a declaration for any `src/` edit of a released package, and an empty frontmatter would pass it. I chose `patch` because the new wording ships. After the build, the marker `objectui#10098` appears once in each of `packages/core/dist/utils/number-display.d.ts`, `packages/i18n/dist/useDisplayLocale.d.ts` and `packages/plugin-report/dist/displayLocale.d.ts`. As a positive control, a phrase that already existed also appears once in each file. `removeComments` is not set in the resolved config of these packages, so TypeScript's default keeps comments. A consumer's editor therefore shows the new contract text, and that deserves a CHANGELOG line.

## Verification (HEAD `4ff6ba9a`)

- **Type-check:** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/i18n --filter @object-ui/plugin-report run type-check` printed `Done` for all three, exit 0. My first attempt ran before the dependency closure was built. It failed with TS6305 (a dependency's `dist` was missing). That was a missing prerequisite, not a type error.
- **Tests:** `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/ packages/i18n/ packages/plugin-report/`, run from the repo root, reported `Test Files 161 passed (161)` and `Tests 2832 passed (2832)`. The 161 files are all the test files in those three paths (72 + 70 + 19).
- **Other gates, all passed:**
  - `pnpm check:control-bytes`: OK.
  - `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations.
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: passed.
  - `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: no findings.
  - `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `pnpm check:unreferenced-sources` and `pnpm check:spec-symbols`: all exit 0.
- **Lint, limited to the 3 touched files:** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` reported 3 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
  - Coverage: `--print-config` shows each file is in scope, with 94 active rules each.
  - Why the limit is safe: no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` resolves for these files, so linting is not type-aware. A comment-only diff therefore cannot change the result for any file it does not touch.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` run is left to CI.
- **Not measured locally:** the full `pnpm test` shards, the repo-wide `pnpm lint`, and the gates that exist only in workflows. CI runs these. One known unrelated failure: `Spec Main Shape Gate` is red on every PR until objectui#10315 lands (tracked on objectui#10287). This diff does not cause it.

## Acceptance notes (not filed)

- `@object-ui/plugin-report` handles a malformed tenant tag in two different ways. `DatasetReportRenderer` formats measures through core's `formatMeasure`, which falls back to the runtime default. `formatValue` and the exporters go through `formatNumberInDisplayLocale`, which falls back to `'en'`. Under the scoped wording, each path follows the contract of the formatter it runs through, so neither violates a contract. I note it here so the next reader does not have to work this out again.
- `.changeset/10020-report-display-locale.md` is pending and not yet released. It says the report "does NOT degrade to a dropped tag". That is accurate about plugin-report's own choice, and it does not call any core behaviour wrong. I left it alone, because it records that other change.
- I added no pin. The only new text is prose, and the retry behaviour was measured here as evidence, not asserted in a test.
